antibodies directed against Z; lytic viral proteins, Z and BMRF1

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (H&E, Z, BMRF1, KLF4, BLIMP1). H&E: H&E histology of a patient-derived OHL biopsy showing ballooned koilocyte-like cells and epithelial hyperplasia with parakeratosis, consistent with classic OHL morphology. Z: IHC for EBV lytic protein Z showing positive nuclear staining in ballooned OHL cells from a patient biopsy, confirming EBV replication in the lesion. BMRF1: IHC for EBV lytic protein BMRF1 showing positive nuclear staining in ballooned OHL cells from a patient biopsy, confirming EBV replication in the lesion. KLF4: IHC for cellular transcription factor KLF4 showing positive nuclear staining in ballooned OHL cells from a patient biopsy; KLF4 expression is not in the vocabulary and is proposed as a finding. BLIMP1: IHC for cellular transcription factor BLIMP1 showing positive nuclear staining in ballooned OHL cells from a patient biopsy; BLIMP1 expression is not in the vocabulary and is proposed as a finding.
panels.attribution_text: Nawandar et al. Differentiation-Dependent KLF4 Expression Promotes Lytic Epstein-Barr Virus Infection in Epithelial Cells.. PLoS pathogens 2015. doi:10.1371/journal.ppat.1005195. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 10.
panels.figure_caption: OHL cells express both KLF4 and BLIMP1. H&E analysis (Image: 40X), and immunohistochemistry analysis was performed on a paraffin-embedded, formalin-fixed biopsy of an oral hairy leukoplakia (OHL) lesion using antibodies directed against Z, BMRF1, KLF4 and BLIMP1 as indicated (Images: 100x of region boxed in H & E stain). Examples of OHL cells, positively staining for each of these proteins, are indicated by black arrows.
in_text_mentions: LF4 and BLIMP1 are also both expressed in the highly lytic OHL lesions that can occur within differentiated tongue epithelium of immunosuppressed patients, we examined KLF4 and BLIMP1 expression in a patient-derived OHL lesion. We confirmed that cells with the morphology typical of OHL cells (“ballooning” cells with a large amount of cytoplasm- see arrows) not only expressed the lytic viral proteins, Z and BMRF1, but also the cellular proteins, KLF4 and BLIMP1 (Fig 10). Collectively, these results suggest that the expression of KLF4 and BLIMP1 correlates with lytic EBV infection in the tongue.

The research using oral hairy leukoplakia lesions for IHC analysis in Fig 10 was approved by Institutional Review Board (IRB) of our institution (University of Wisconsin Madison), as well as the IRB of our collaborating institution (University of California, San Francisco). All adult subjects provided written informed consent (and no children were in the study). panels.figure_caption: A,B: Hyperparakeratinized stratified squamous epithelium with “balloon cells”, arrowhead. C: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in situ hybridization positive in epithelial cell nuclei.
in_text_mentions: Detox Pro® mouthwash was prescripted twice a day, for fifteen days. After three months, the lesions did not regress. So, an incisional biopsy was performed. Anatomopathological examination revealed the presence of epithelial hyperplasia and extensive hyperparakeratosis with bacterial colonies on the surface. In the squamous epithelium, “ballooned” cells and nuclei with chromatin condensation in the “beading” pattern of the nuclear membrane were observed. These data associated with the positive immunohistochemical examination for anti-EBV in the cells resulted in the diagnosis of OHL, (Fig. 2).

plate_findings.evidence: cells with opaque nucleus, and perinuclear halo

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Low-power H&E histopathology of an OHL biopsy showing the classic epithelial hyperplasia, koilocyte-like ballooned cells, and viral cytopathic nuclear changes; the article title and in-text mention attribute the figure to oral hairy leukoplakia. B: High-power H&E histopathology of the same OHL biopsy explicitly showing koilocyte-like ballooned epithelial cells, a classic histologic manifestation of oral hairy leukoplakia. C: Low-power in situ hybridization of the OHL biopsy shows EBV positivity, confirming the disease attribution in the article focused on EBV in situ hybridization for oral hairy leukoplakia. D: High-power in situ hybridization of the OHL biopsy shows EBV positivity, the diagnostic virologic manifestation supporting oral hairy leukoplakia.

Cohen's kappa coefficient between clinical examination and in situ hybridization was 0.78.
